blocks: Congress passed a law to stop fake robocalls. Your phone still rings. Here is why.
In twenty nineteen, there were fifty-eight and a half billion robocalls, by YouMail's estimate.
That December, the TRACED Act was signed. Its key idea is STIR SHAKEN, a digital signature for phone calls. The carrier that starts the call signs the number. The carrier that receives it checks it.
And it has teeth. In twenty twenty-one, the FCC fined two Texas telemarketers two hundred twenty-five million dollars, for about one billion spoofed calls.
But in twenty twenty-five, YouMail still estimates about fifty-two and a half billion robocalls. The law did not shrink the problem. It leveled off.
The law made the fake number harder to hide. It did not make your phone go quiet.
The case that started it all, a hundred twenty million dollar fine, is on The Rule Changed.
